Subject: SDK proto + acceptance criteria for streaming / funcalls / embeddings

Hi Elliot — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have a shared checklist going into the POC. Please flag anything I missed.

High-level goals you described:
- Reduce time-to-answer for long-context troubleshooting queries across knowledge base + logs (target: median < 120ms for short queries; p95 < 350ms for common queries).
- Combine semantic search (embeddings) + reranking to improve recall for multi-document incidents.
- Reliable structured outputs (JSON) for downstream automation (ticket triage fields).

Key pain points you called out:
- Current vendor has brittle function-calling outputs (fields missing / inconsistent types).
- Long-form outputs time out in high-concurrency bursts (especially during incident windows).
- Security: all PII must be redacted prior to storage; production traffic must run in a VPC with customer-managed keys.

Proposed technical approach (what Redwood will validate during POC):
1) SDK prototype: provide a small Node + Python SDK patch that demonstrates streaming tokens + function calling in the same session. We'll include an example with on-the-fly JSON schema enforcement and a fallback to structured extractor when parsing fails.
2) Embeddings + rerank: demo a two-stage pipeline (approximate nearest neighbors using embeddings -> model-based reranker) with an example dataset you provide (logs + KB).
3) Performance targets and SLOs: define token-level batching and KV-cache policies to hit your p95 latency target during a 100 rps sustained workload.
4) Security checklist: VPC deployment option + KMS integration; SOC2 evidence we'll surface.

Acceptance criteria (please confirm):
- Functional: Function call outputs conform to the agreed JSON schema in >= 95% of sample prompts (on your test set).
- Latency: Under the POC workload, p95 text-gen latency for 256-token responses is < 350ms.
- Cost: Estimated per-1M token cost under the POC configuration (we'll provide a ballpark in the next doc).
- Security: Demonstrate encrypted transit + no persistent retention of raw PII in the demo environment.

Immediate next steps (owners & timeline):
- Sergio: deliver SDK prototype + example app by Jun 18 (attachment: redwood-sdk-proposal-pt1.pdf).
- Ben: baseline perf matrix and recommended batching config by Jun 18.
- Elliot / StormGrid: share sample dataset (logs + 200 KB articles) and a short list of critical fields for the function-call JSON schema by EOD Jun 17.
- Monica: coordinate procurement contact if we need an NDA / PO for the POC.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-proposal-pt1.pdf (short design + example calls)

Open items for your confirmation:
- Do you want streamed partial JSON objects (server-sent-chunks) or wait-for-complete structured output? (streaming can reduce perceived latency but requires tolerant parsers).
- Any firewall/VPN constraints for the POC environment?

Thanks — I can hop back on a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the SDK demo if that's easiest.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

Sergio — this is great, thanks for the clear breakdown. A few quick confirmations and clarifications: 

- Acceptance criteria: we agree with the functional + latency targets. For JSON schema matching, can we add a tolerance for auxiliary keys (i.e., allow extra keys so long as required fields are present and typed correctly)?
- Streaming vs complete JSON: prefer streamed partials for user-facing consoles (so we can show progressive updates) but need a guaranteed final validated payload for automation. If Redwood can provide both (streamed tokens + a validated final JSON object) that would be ideal.
- Dataset: attaching an export (stormgrid-poc-reqs.xlsx) with sample logs and a list of 12 critical fields. We'll also drop a 2GB sample bundle to the Drive folder you shared by EOD.

Procurement: looping in our platform procurement alias (platform@stormgrid.com) — we'll need a short SOW + standard PO process. Any templates?

Schedule: Jun 17 dataset drop (we'll aim for morning). Jun 18 SDK prototype demo at 10:00 PT works for our team — please send an invite.

Elliot / Sergio — quick technical notes from my side ahead of the demo: 

1) SDK approach: we'll ship a small change to our streaming client that emits structured JSON events as they are produced and then a single validation pass at the end. Example flow: "emit partial tokens -> emit partial JSON fragments with metadata -> final validated object with signature". That pattern should give you progressive UI + a guaranteed canonical payload for automation.

2) Reranking: for the POC we'll use 1536-d embeddings (float16 quantized for speed) + an HNSW index. We'll run an internal sweep on nearest-neighbor recall vs top-k for your sample KB and include a suggested top-k and reranker threshold in the perf matrix.

3) Latency tuning: recommend starting with a small batch size (dynamic batching up to 16 requests) and aggressive KV-cache warmup for recurrent session IDs (your troubleshooting flows reuse context heavily). We'll validate p95 at 100 rps synthetic load. 

4) Security: Monica will coordinate the VPC onboarding. For the POC we can run in a dedicated VPC in our US-west region with a customer-managed KMS key and no retention of raw queries longer than 24 hours (configurable).

I'll attach a short perf baseline and example curl + Python snippets in the Drive folder before the demo. Looking forward to the call on Jun 18 at 10:00 PT.

-Ben
